title: React Developer - Mid-level
description: Role-specific fundamentals and practical troubleshooting. 8 MCQs and 3 written scenarios; no coding questions.
reviewerInstructions: Score each written response against its rubric. Award points for specific, technically sound reasoning and trade-offs. Notes are optional. Publish only after every criterion is scored. The recommendation is a human judgment; this application does not make hiring decisions.

items.text: How should an array stored in React state be updated?
choices: Mutate the existing array and keep its reference
Create an updated array and pass it to the state setter
Assign directly to the state variable
items.correctAnswer: Create an updated array and pass it to the state setter
items.explanation: Treat state arrays as read-only; supply a new array when changing their contents.

items.text: What is the main purpose of a stable key when rendering a changing React list?
choices: Identify corresponding list items between renders
items.correctAnswer: Identify corresponding list items between renders
items.explanation: Stable keys let React match list items when items move, are inserted, or are removed.

items.text: An Effect subscribes to an external event source. What should its cleanup do?
items.explanation: Effect cleanup should undo the setup so subscriptions do not accumulate.

items.text: What happens when a listed Effect dependency changes between renders?
choices: React may re-synchronize the Effect after cleanup
The component can never render again
items.correctAnswer: React may re-synchronize the Effect after cleanup
items.explanation: React compares dependencies and re-synchronizes an Effect when its dependencies change.

items.text: Which update uses the pending previous state when incrementing a counter?
items.explanation: A functional updater calculates the next state from the pending previous state.

items.text: Which element is the best default for an action a user can activate by keyboard?
choices: A div with only an onClick handler
A span with only a color change
A paragraph with a pointer cursor
items.explanation: Native buttons provide keyboard activation and button semantics; custom interactions need equivalent accessibility support.

items.text: Where should a browser application enforce authorization for protected API data?
choices: In the API server for each protected request
Only in a React component name
items.correctAnswer: In the API server for each protected request
items.explanation: Browser UI restrictions cannot replace server-side authorization.

items.text: What should an accessible asynchronous results screen distinguish?
choices: Only the number of CSS files
Loading, successful empty results, data and errors
items.correctAnswer: Loading, successful empty results, data and errors
items.explanation: Distinct request states let users understand progress, recover from errors and recognize valid empty results.

items.text: A React search screen sometimes shows results for an older query. Explain the state model, request lifecycle, error handling and tests you would use.

rubric.label: Correctness and lifecycle
rubric.guidance: 0: ignores race conditions. 1-4: basic fetching. 5-7: cleanup or request identity guards, dependency handling and clear state ownership. 8-10: discusses cancellation limits, caching and competing requests.

rubric.label: Testing and user experience
rubric.guidance: 0: no tests. 1-4: happy path only. 5-7: out-of-order responses, error/empty/loading states and retry. 8-10: covers accessibility announcements and fast user input.

items.text: A list of 5,000 editable items loses input focus and renders slowly. Describe how you would diagnose it and improve performance without losing user edits.

rubric.label: Identity and state ownership
rubric.guidance: 0: unsafe mutation or unstable identity. 1-4: basic controlled inputs. 5-7: stable keys, immutable updates and localized state. 8-10: explains reconciliation, stale state and preserving in-progress edits.

rubric.label: Measured performance and accessibility
rubric.guidance: 0: no plan. 1-4: generic memoization. 5-7: profiling, virtualization/pagination and measured memoization. 8-10: tests focus, keyboard navigation and rendering costs.

items.text: Design an accessible checkout form using a protected API. Explain validation, preventing duplicate orders, security boundaries and failure recovery.

rubric.label: Form correctness and security
rubric.guidance: 0: trusts client authorization. 1-4: basic form. 5-7: labeled inputs, field/server validation and server authorization. 8-10: handles sensitive data, idempotency and concurrency boundaries.

rubric.label: Recovery and verification
rubric.guidance: 0: ignores failures. 1-4: generic alerts. 5-7: loading and retry states, preserved inputs and integration tests. 8-10: tests keyboard operation, error focus and ambiguous API outcomes.
